title: A molecular switch for coordinating kinesin and dynein transport of mitochondrial cargo.
data_url: https://zenodo.org/records/20263176 (code only); supplement = one PDF + two movies

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the Europe PMC supplement archive (50.9 MB): it holds one 20.6 MB PDF of supplementary figures (~44 pages), two movies and the four main figure images - zero spreadsheets or text tables. Downloaded and unzipped all three Zenodo deposits (8 KB, 239 KB, 668 KB): all are software (MIT / BSD-3 licence). Opened every spreadsheet and CSV inside them with pandas - config_V3.xlsx, config_round2_V3.xlsx, Comparisons_table_v3.xlsx and coordinate_overrides.csv contain only plate/well identifiers per figure panel (e.g. 'TRAK1 helix muts' sheet, 4 rows x 4 columns of well codes), image-segmentation thresholds, and pixel coordinate overrides - no measured quantities. Grepped the full open-access text: no PRIDE, MassIVE, ProteomeXchange, BioStudies accession, and no 'Table S'/'Data S'/'source data' mention anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design and effect sizes (speeds ~1.02-1.07 micrometres/second; n = 21 cells / 573 tracks for TRAK1, n = 47 cells for TRAK2; nested ANOVA with n = 8 plates) are read from the text and figure legends only. I could not extract text from the 20.6 MB supplementary PDF (no pdftotext on this machine), so I infer it is figures-plus-legends from its file name, page count and the absence of any table reference in the article text.

a1_downloadable.note: No measurement data is downloadable. The data availability statement says only 'All data are available in the main text or the supplementary materials' and 'reagents available upon reasonable request'; the supplement is a figures PDF plus movies, and the three Zenodo DOIs are analysis code whose README states 'Raw ND2 files are not included' (ND2 = Nikon microscope image format). Quantified per-cell values exist only as dots inside figure panels.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The prediction target - how far a synthetic cargo moves toward the cell periphery versus the nucleus for each TRAK (trafficking kinesin-binding protein) variant - is not a column anywhere. It would have to be reconstructed by re-running the authors' image pipeline on microscope images that were never deposited, or by digitising plotted points from a PDF.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not reached in effect, but the inputs (TRAK1/TRAK2 protein sequences, UniProt Q9UPV9 / O60296) are trivially obtainable from UniProt; the mutations are named in the text.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in figure legends (micrometres/second for speeds, Gini coefficient and edge-spot fraction for accumulation), but there is no table in which to apply them.

a5_enough_rows.note: The experimental unit is the construct/condition, and the configuration sheets enumerate roughly 10-25 of them (no TRAK, TRAK1, TRAK2, chimera, DRH mutants, Spindly mutants, S84A/S84E, MAPK9 knockdown, arsenite) with 3-9 plate replicates each - orders of magnitude under the ~400-1,500 row bar. Counted from the Zenodo comparison sheets I opened.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything that exists is small (51 MB supplement, under 1 MB of code), so size is not the problem - the absence of data is.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no deposited counts exist to check against the paper's n values.

a8_label_provenance.note: Where labels exist in the figures they come from real fluorescence microscopy of live cells, not from a model's output - so provenance is clean in principle; it is availability that fails.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would have been the natural backbone for a sequence-to-directionality model
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for a few dozen short helix sequences, but there is no label table to fit a head on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the paper's own code is MIT/BSD-3

integration.partner_dataset: UniProt / AlphaFold DB (predicted structures) for dynein activating adaptors, joinable on UniProt accession
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Could a sequence model predict, across all dynein activating adaptors, whether a given regulatory helix keeps dynein off or lets it on? - a real question, but this paper contributes about a dozen measured variants toward it, far too few to train or even to test on.

controls.positive_control: Wild-type TRAK1 (peripheral, kinesin-biased) versus wild-type TRAK2 (perinuclear, dynein-biased) is a clean known contrast a model must recover - but it is only two data points.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be meaningless at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: Other dynein adaptor papers (BICD2, Spindly, HOOK3) report directionality for a handful of constructs each, but assays and readouts differ and none share this paper's quantification.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with roughly a dozen engineered TRAK constructs and no deposited per-cell measurements, any model would be describing a handful of hand-picked mutations rather than predicting anything.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an adaptor protein's regulatory helix sequence to predict whether its cargo moves outward or inward in the cell.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model the amino-acid sequence of the regulatory helix region of mitochondrial adaptor proteins (TRAK1 and TRAK2 and their engineered mutants). Verified count of distinct measured constructs: roughly 10-25, read off the deposited plate-comparison sheets.
plain_idea.predict: The direction of cargo movement - toward the cell edge (kinesin-driven) or toward the nucleus (dynein-driven) - measured by live fluorescence microscopy of a synthetic 60-subunit cargo particle and summarised as a peripheral-versus-perinuclear accumulation score.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cell biologists studying mitochondrial positioning in neurons would want a rule for which adaptor sequences bias transport inward, since mitochondrial mispositioning causes fatal encephalopathy when TRAK1 is mutated. But that rule needs hundreds of measured variants, and this paper deposits none.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: fine-tune a frozen protein language model to predict kinesin-versus-dynein transport bias from adaptor helix sequence, using this paper's AlphaFold2-guided mutagenesis series as labels. The labels were never deposited in machine-readable form and number a dozen or so constructs, so neither training nor honest evaluation is possible.

effort.compute_note: Sizes are measured from the files I downloaded (50.9 MB supplement, 0.9 MB of code). Time estimates are null because there is no feature/label table to build.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the supplement and open the Zenodo deposits - five minutes shows the supplement is a figures PDF and the deposits are code with configuration spreadsheets, not measurements. That check killed it.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 first, then A2 and A5. This is a beautiful mechanistic cell-biology paper whose entire quantitative output lives inside figure panels: the 50.9 MB supplement is one PDF plus two movies, the three Zenodo DOIs are analysis code (8-668 KB, MIT/BSD) whose spreadsheets hold only plate/well codes and segmentation thresholds, and the README says the raw microscope images are not included. Even if the images existed, the experimental unit is the construct and there are roughly 10-25 of them. No phosphoproteomics accession (PRIDE/MassIVE/ProteomeXchange) appears anywhere in the text either. Nothing to model.
